risks.title: Biomass feedstock supply reliability insufficient
risks.description: Insufficient quantity of biomass feedstock available year-round to sustain continuous FT plant operation at design capacity, due to seasonal availability, competing demand, or supply chain immaturity.
risks.early_warning_signals: Lower-than-expected contracted volumes; suppliers missing delivery schedules; spot-market price spikes for biomass
risks.mitigation: Diversify feedstock types (forestry residue, agricultural residue, energy crops); secure long-term offtake agreements with multiple suppliers; build on-site storage buffer for 30-60 days
risks.contingency: Procure supplemental biomass from alternative geographies; reduce plant throughput; activate biomass import arrangements

risks.title: Moisture content variability in biomass feedstock
risks.description: Seasonal moisture content in biomass ranges from 15% (dry summer) to 40% (wet winter), causing inconsistent gasification performance, lower cold gas efficiency, and increased oxidant consumption.
risks.early_warning_signals: Moisture analysis on incoming loads exceeding 30%; gasifier temperature fluctuations; syngas composition drift
risks.mitigation: Install covered storage to shield feedstock from rain; mix wet and dry batches to average moisture; pre-drying step using low-grade waste heat
risks.contingency: Increase oxidant flow to compensate; reduce feed rate; reject loads above 40% moisture

risks.title: Biomass ash content exceeds gasifier design limits
risks.description: High ash content in biomass (especially agricultural residues like straw/stover) leads to increased slagging, fouling, ash handling burden, and reduced carbon conversion efficiency.
risks.early_warning_signals: Ash analysis on delivered feedstock above 8% wt; increased bottom ash discharge frequency; gasifier pressure drop rising
risks.mitigation: Specify maximum ash content in feedstock contracts; blend low-ash with high-ash feedstocks; install ash removal system with design margin for 20% overcapacity
risks.contingency: Reject out-of-spec loads; source alternative low-ash feedstock; install additional ash handling equipment

risks.title: Alkali metal content causes bed agglomeration
risks.description: Potassium and sodium in biomass ash form low-melting-point eutectics in the fluidised bed gasifier, causing defluidisation, agglomeration, and unscheduled shutdowns.
risks.early_warning_signals: Rising bed pressure drop; temperature profile flattening across bed; visual agglomerates in bottom ash
risks.mitigation: Pre-leach biomass to remove alkali metals; use alkali-adsorbing bed materials (e.g., dolomite); maintain bed temperature below ash softening point
risks.contingency: Replace bed material on emergency basis; switch to less problematic feedstock; partial shut down for bed replacement

risks.title: Contaminants in biomass exceed gasifier tolerance
risks.description: Chlorine, sulfur, nitrogen, and heavy metals in feedstock cause corrosion, emissions issues, and increased syngas cleanup burden, degrading downstream catalyst life.
risks.early_warning_signals: Elevated HCl, H2S, or NH3 in syngas analysis; corrosion probe readings increasing; catalyst deactivation rate accelerating
risks.mitigation: Establish strict feedstock contaminant specifications; periodic batch testing before acceptance; blend contaminated batches with cleaner feedstock
risks.contingency: Reject out-of-spec loads; increase guard bed replacement frequency; install additional scrubber capacity

risks.title: Biomass feedstock price volatility
risks.description: Spot-market prices for biomass fluctuate significantly due to competing uses (power generation, pellets, animal bedding), weather events, and policy changes, eroding project economics.
risks.early_warning_signals: Commodity price indices trending upward; competing biomass plants announcing new capacity; policy incentives shifting
risks.mitigation: Long-term fixed-price contracts with escalation clauses; forward hedging via biomass commodity markets; vertical integration through feedstock production
risks.contingency: Activate price renegotiation clauses; draw on feedstock inventory buffer; reduce plant utilisation to match affordable supply

risks.title: Seasonal interruption of biomass supply
risks.description: Biomass availability is seasonally constrained — harvesting windows are limited (e.g., post-harvest season lasting 8-12 weeks) and weather-dependent, causing winter supply gaps.
risks.early_warning_signals: Harvest yield forecasts below plan; wet weather delaying collection; storage drawdown rate exceeding replenishment
risks.mitigation: Build storage capacity for 90 days of operation; diversify geographic sourcing to offset regional seasons; secure multiple harvest windows
risks.contingency: Use alternative feedstock types available off-season; import biomass from other regions/countries; schedule plant maintenance during low-supply periods

risks.title: Biomass storage degradation (self-heating and mould)
risks.description: Biomass stored in piles undergoes microbial degradation, self-heating, dry matter loss (5-20%), and mould growth, reducing energy content and creating HSE hazards (spontaneous combustion risk).
risks.early_warning_signals: Temperature rise inside storage piles; visible mould/fungal growth; odour of decomposition; weight loss in stored inventory
risks.mitigation: Limit pile height and implement active aeration; monitor internal temperature with thermocouple arrays; first-in-first-out stock rotation; use covered storage
risks.contingency: Discard degraded material; accelerate stock rotation; reduce pile size; increase aeration rate

risks.title: Competing demand for biomass from other sectors
risks.description: Power generation, heating, biofuel, and pellet industries compete for the same biomass resource, driving up prices and reducing availability as the SAF industry scales.
risks.early_warning_signals: New biomass-using facilities announced in the region; biomass price rising faster than inflation; permits for new biomass suppliers being acquired
risks.mitigation: Secure long-term exclusive contracts; develop dedicated biomass supply chains (energy crops); participate in regional biomass resource planning
risks.contingency: Feedstock diversification into non-competing sources (e.g., municipal solid waste fraction); import from less competitive markets

risks.title: Feedstock particle size distribution out of spec
risks.description: Inconsistent particle size (too large or too fine) from different suppliers causes gasifier feed system blockages, poor fluidisation, or excessive carryover into the syngas train.
risks.early_warning_signals: Feed system bridging/jamming; gasifier pressure fluctuations; increased particulate carryover to cyclones
risks.mitigation: Specify particle size distribution in feedstock contracts; install pre-processing (grinding/screening) at plant reception; blend size fractions to target distribution
risks.contingency: Reject non-compliant loads; adjust grinder settings; install additional screening capacity

risks.title: Gasification technology not demonstrated at scale for this feedstock
risks.description: The selected gasification technology (e.g., fluidised bed, entrained flow) has not been commercially proven at the required scale (500+ tpd) with the specific biomass feedstock type, creating technology risk.
risks.early_warning_signals: Pilot/demo plant results below projections; vendor unable to provide reference plants with similar feedstock; extended ramp-up period
risks.mitigation: Conduct extended feedstock testing at pilot/demo scale; include technology performance guarantees in EPC contract; license proven gasifier design with feedstock flexibility
risks.contingency: Engage technology vendor for on-site support during commissioning; design modular trains to de-risk scale-up; maintain option for alternative gasifier technology

risks.title: Refractory erosion and failure in gasifier
risks.description: High-temperature gasifier refractory lining erodes due to slag attack, thermal cycling, and mechanical abrasion from feedstock, leading to hot spots, shell overheating, and premature replacement.
risks.early_warning_signals: Rising external shell temperature; refractory thickness below design minimum at inspection; increased heat loss through wall
risks.mitigation: Select high-alumina/silicon-carbide refractory designed for biomass ash; implement thermocouple monitoring embedded in refractory; schedule routine refractory inspections
risks.contingency: Hot patch repair during planned maintenance; reduce operating temperature; replace refractory on expedited schedule

risks.title: Slagging and agglomeration in fluidised bed gasifier
risks.description: Biomass ash with low melting point causes bed particles to stick together forming agglomerates, leading to defluidisation, poor gas-solid contact, and forced shutdowns.
risks.early_warning_signals: Increasing bed pressure drop; temperature differential across bed increasing; visual agglomerates in bed drain samples
risks.mitigation: Maintain bed temperature 50-100°C below ash softening point; use dolomite/limestone bed additive to raise eutectic melting temperature; install online bed sampling system
risks.contingency: Partial bed replacement; reduce steam/oxygen ratio to lower temperature; emergency shutdown for full bed replacement

risks.title: Low carbon conversion in gasifier
risks.description: Carbon conversion below design (e.g., <95%) due to poor gas-solid contacting, short residence time, or refractory char, reducing overall plant efficiency and increasing char disposal costs.
risks.early_warning_signals: Carbon content in bottom ash >5%; syngas yield below design; char recycle rate increasing
risks.mitigation: Optimise steam/oxygen ratio and temperature profile; implement char recycle to increase residence time; improve feedstock preparation for better reactivity
risks.contingency: Adjust operating parameters (higher temperature, longer residence time); install additional char recycle loop; blend more reactive feedstock

risks.title: Syngas quality below design — low H2/CO ratio
risks.description: Product syngas H2/CO ratio below the FT synthesis requirement (~0.6-0.7 for iron catalyst, higher for cobalt), requiring additional water-gas shift, increasing capital and operating costs.
risks.early_warning_signals: Syngas H2/CO ratio consistently below 0.5; increased steam injection yielding marginal improvement; downstream shift reactor duty above design
risks.mitigation: Incorporate water-gas shift reactor in design with capacity margin; optimise gasifier steam/oxygen ratio; select FT catalyst tolerant to lower H2/CO ratio (iron-based)
risks.contingency: Add supplemental shift catalyst; reduce FT throughput to match available H2; blend with external H2 source

risks.title: Syngas quality below design — high methane slip
risks.description: Excessive methane in syngas (above design specification of <2 vol%) reduces FT reactor productivity and increases off-gas recycle load, lowering overall carbon efficiency.
risks.early_warning_signals: CH4 concentration in syngas >3%; FT reactor per-pass conversion declining; purge gas methane content increasing
risks.mitigation: Optimise gasifier temperature (higher temperature reduces CH4); install catalytic tar reformer with CH4 reforming capability; incorporate membrane separation for CH4 removal
risks.contingency: Reform CH4 in separate reformer before FT; increase purge rate from FT loop; adjust catalyst formulation for higher CH4 tolerance

risks.title: High nitrogen content in syngas from air-blown gasification
risks.description: Use of air as oxidant introduces nitrogen into syngas, diluting the FT feed, increasing compression costs, and reducing reactor productivity per unit volume.
risks.early_warning_signals: Syngas N2 concentration above 5%; FT reactor volumetric productivity below design; purge compressor load excessive
risks.mitigation: Use oxygen-blown gasification (ASU supplied); if air-blown, design FT loop for higher purge rate; incorporate N2 removal membrane
risks.contingency: Increase purge rate accepting some yield loss; add N2 rejection system; reduce plant throughput to manage diluent load

risks.title: Oxidant purity insufficient for gasification
risks.description: Air Separation Unit (ASU) delivers oxygen purity below design spec (e.g., <95%), introducing argon and nitrogen into syngas, reducing FT reactor efficiency.
risks.early_warning_signals: Oxygen purity trending below 95%; increasing argon in syngas; ASU performance indicators degrading
risks.mitigation: Specify minimum 95% oxygen purity in ASU contract; implement online oxygen purity monitoring; maintain ASU with regular performance testing
risks.contingency: Increase ASU purge rate; operate air-blown mode as fallback; blend with high-purity oxygen from backup supply

risks.title: Gasifier feed system plugging
risks.description: Biomass bridging, rat-holing, or plugging in lock hoppers, screw feeders, or pneumatic injection lines causes feed interruptions, gasifier pressure fluctuations, and process trips.
risks.early_warning_signals: Feed rate fluctuations; lock hopper pressure equalisation delays; increasing torque on screw feeders
risks.mitigation: Design feed system with multiple redundant injection points; use live-bottom hoppers with agitators; maintain smooth and consistent particle size distribution
risks.contingency: Operate with redundant feed line; clear plugged lines with purge gas; manual intervention to dislodge bridges

risks.title: Tar fouling and filter blocking in syngas cleanup
risks.description: Heavy tars from biomass gasification condense on downstream filter elements and heat exchangers, causing pressure drop buildup, fouling, and reduced syngas availability.
risks.early_warning_signals: Candle filter differential pressure rising; heat exchanger U-value declining; visible tar deposits in downstream piping
risks.mitigation: Operate gasifier at high temperature (>850°C) to minimise tar formation; install catalytic tar reformer upstream of filters; design filters with pulsed back-flushing and high-temperature operation
risks.contingency: Increase back-flush frequency; replace filter elements on accelerated schedule; install guard filter upstream of critical equipment

risks.title: Tar reformer catalyst deactivation by sulfur and chlorine
risks.description: Sulfur (H2S) and chlorine (HCl) from biomass gasification poison the tar reforming catalyst (typically Ni-based), reducing its activity for tar cracking and methane reforming.
risks.early_warning_signals: Increasing tar slip downstream of reformer; rising CH4 concentration in syngas; catalyst bed temperature profile shift
risks.mitigation: Install sulfur/chlorine guard bed upstream of tar reformer; use sulfur-tolerant catalyst formulation (e.g., La-Ni, noble metal promoted); maintain H2S < 20 ppmv to reformer
risks.contingency: Replace tar reformer catalyst on expedited schedule; increase reformer operating temperature; install additional guard bed capacity

risks.title: Sulfur breakthrough poisoning FT catalyst
risks.description: Sulfur compounds (H2S, COS, mercaptans) breaking through the syngas cleanup train deactivate the FT catalyst permanently, requiring premature catalyst replacement and causing major economic loss.
risks.early_warning_signals: H2S > 50 ppbv at FT reactor inlet; FT CO conversion rate declining; catalyst activity trending downward
risks.mitigation: Multi-layer sulfur removal (ZnO + activated carbon + guard bed with final polishing); online H2S analysis with automatic shutdown at >100 ppbv; dual guard beds in series with lead/lag configuration
risks.contingency: Isolate FT reactor on sulfur breakthrough alarm; replace guard bed immediately; evaluate FT catalyst damage and replace if necessary

risks.title: Chlorine breakthrough causing corrosion and catalyst poisoning
risks.description: HCl breaking through the cleanup train causes corrosion of downstream equipment (stainless steel, heat exchangers) and permanent poisoning of FT and hydroprocessing catalysts.
risks.early_warning_signals: Chloride detected in syngas condensate; corrosion probe readings elevated; FT catalyst activity decline despite H2S < 50 ppbv
risks.mitigation: Install dedicated HCl removal (sodium aluminate or promoted activated carbon) upstream of sulfur removal; maintain chloride guard bed with online monitoring; use corrosion-resistant materials downstream
risks.contingency: Replace chloride guard bed immediately; inspect downstream equipment for corrosion damage; replace poisoned catalyst in FT and hydroprocessing

risks.title: Particulate carryover damaging downstream equipment
risks.description: Fine particulates (ash, char, bed material) passing through cyclones and filters erode compressor blades, foul heat exchangers, and accumulate in FT reactors, degrading performance.
risks.early_warning_signals: Particulate loading in syngas >5 mg/Nm3; compressor vibration increasing; heat exchanger fouling factor rising
risks.mitigation: Design high-efficiency cyclone train followed by ceramic candle filters rated for <1 mg/Nm3; install particulate guard bed; online particulate monitoring via laser diffraction
risks.contingency: Replace/regenerate filter elements; install additional polishing filter; clean affected equipment during maintenance turnaround

risks.title: Guard bed premature exhaustion requiring frequent changeouts
risks.description: Guard beds (ZnO, activated carbon, Cu-promoted beds) become saturated with contaminants faster than design due to higher-than-expected inlet loads, causing frequent operational interruptions.
risks.early_warning_signals: Breakthrough curve shifting earlier than expected; bed life 30%+ below design; frequent analysis showing guard bed approaching saturation
risks.mitigation: Design guard bed with 50% excess capacity; install dual lead/lag vessels for online changeout; upstream polishing to reduce inlet contaminant load
risks.contingency: Increase guard bed changeout frequency; replace with higher-capacity sorbent; install additional polishing stage upstream

risks.title: FT catalyst deactivation by sulfur poisoning
risks.description: Sub-ppmv level H2S reaching the FT reactor permanently deactivates cobalt or iron FT catalyst, requiring premature catalyst replacement at high cost ($50-100M per full load).
risks.early_warning_signals: Measurable H2S at FT inlet; CO conversion decline of 0.5-1% per week; catalyst bed temperature trending upward to maintain conversion
risks.mitigation: Maintain H2S < 10 ppbv with multi-layer Polish guard bed; install online sulfur analyser with automatic isolation valve; periodic catalyst activity testing
risks.contingency: Replace poisoned FT catalyst batch; install additional sulfur guard capacity; recover precious metals from spent catalyst

risks.title: FT catalyst deactivation by carbon deposition
risks.description: Carbon deposition (coking) on FT catalyst surface blocks active sites, reduces catalyst lifetime (target 3-5 years), and increases reactor pressure drop in fixed-bed configurations.
risks.early_warning_signals: Rising pressure drop across reactor; catalyst bed void fraction declining; CO conversion dropping at constant temperature; H2 consumption per CO converted increasing
risks.mitigation: Maintain H2/CO ratio above 0.6; use catalyst with optimised pore structure to resist coking; periodic regeneration with hydrogen-rich gas
risks.contingency: Replace coked catalyst; adjust H2/CO ratio to suppress coking; implement hydrogen stripping regeneration cycle

risks.title: FT catalyst attrition in slurry reactor
risks.description: Cobalt or iron catalyst particles in slurry bubble-column reactors break down due to mechanical attrition, producing fines that are difficult to separate from wax, leading to catalyst loss and product contamination.
risks.early_warning_signals: Fines concentration in wax product increasing; catalyst particle size distribution shifting finer; wax filtration pressure rising
risks.mitigation: Use high attrition-resistant catalyst (spray-dried or supported); optimise slurry circulation rate and gas velocity; install secondary fines separation (hydrocyclones, magnetic separation)
risks.contingency: Increase wax filtration frequency; replace attrited catalyst; install additional fines removal equipment

risks.title: FT reactor temperature runaway
risks.description: Exothermic FT reaction (ΔH = -165 kJ/mol CO) can lead to temperature runaway if heat removal fails, causing catalyst deactivation, reactor damage, and potential safety incident.
risks.early_warning_signals: Localised hot spots in catalyst bed; cooling water temperature rise; temperature differential across reactor increasing; CO conversion spike
risks.mitigation: Design with adequate heat removal surface area; multiple independent cooling coils; interlock on high temperature differential; catalyst dilution with inert material in hot zones
risks.contingency: Automatic reactor shutdown on high-high temperature; depressurise and inert; inspect reactor internals before restart

risks.title: Slurry separation — wax filtration issues
risks.description: Inefficient separation of liquid wax from slurry catalyst fines leads to catalyst carryover into downstream hydroprocessing, product contamination, and catalyst loss.
risks.early_warning_signals: Catalyst fines in wax filter feed increasing; filter cake solids content too high; filter cycle time decreasing; iron/cobalt found in hydroprocessing feed
risks.mitigation: Install cross-flow filtration or magnetic separation; maintain catalyst particle size > 20 microns; design redundant filter train for online cleaning
risks.contingency: Replace filter elements with finer mesh; add polishing centrifuge; hydrocyclone for fines recovery

risks.title: Wax and fines accumulation in FT reactor
risks.description: Accumulation of high-molecular-weight wax and catalyst fines inside the FT reactor reduces active volume, increases pressure drop, and degrades gas-liquid mass transfer.
risks.early_warning_signals: Reactor liquid level rising; pressure drop across reactor increasing; CO conversion declining at same conditions
risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous wax removal via internal filter; periodic catalyst/wax withdrawal and fresh catalyst addition; design with internal liquid recirculation to suspend solids
risks.contingency: Increase wax withdrawal rate; drain and replace reactor contents; clean reactor internals during turnaround

risks.title: Low selectivity to C5+ hydrocarbons
risks.description: FT catalyst produces more methane and light gases (C1-C4) than design, reducing the yield of valuable liquid hydrocarbon products and degrading overall carbon efficiency.
risks.early_warning_signals: CH4 selectivity > 10%; C5+ selectivity < 85%; ASF distribution shifting to lighter products
risks.mitigation: Optimise reactor temperature (lower temperature favours heavier products); use promoter to enhance C5+ selectivity (e.g., Re on Co); maintain optimal H2/CO ratio
risks.contingency: Reduce reactor temperature; replace catalyst with more selective formulation; increase recycle of light ends to FT reactor for chain growth

risks.title: Iron catalyst water-gas shift complications
risks.description: Iron-based FT catalyst has significant WGS activity, consuming CO and producing CO2, reducing carbon efficiency to liquid products and increasing CO2 venting/capture load.
risks.early_warning_signals: CO2 concentration in FT off-gas above 15%; CO conversion higher than expected but liquid yield lower; carbon balance closure declining
risks.mitigation: Use cobalt catalyst instead of iron (low WGS activity) if syngas H2/CO ratio is adequate; optimise catalyst formulation to suppress WGS (alkali promotion controlled); design for CO2 capture
risks.contingency: Install CO2 removal from recycle loop; increase purge rate to manage CO2; consider carbon capture and storage/utilization

risks.title: Low jet fuel yield — excess cracking to gas and naphtha
risks.description: Hydroprocessing of FT wax produces excessive light products (C1-C4 gas, C5-C9 naphtha) at the expense of the target jet fraction (C9-C15), reducing SAF yield well below design target.
risks.early_warning_signals: Naphtha yield above design; jet fraction C9-C15 below 50% of product slate; product distillation curve lighter than target
risks.mitigation: Optimise hydrocracker operating temperature and pressure; use selective catalyst formulation designed for maximum jet; implement product recycle for further conversion of naphtha to jet
risks.contingency: Adjust operating severity (lower temperature, higher pressure); replace catalyst with more selective type; upgrade naphtha via oligomerisation to jet range

risks.title: High hydrogen consumption in hydroprocessing
risks.description: Hydrocracking and hydroisomerisation of FT wax consume more H2 than design estimate (typically 150-250 Nm3/bbl), increasing operating cost and requiring additional H2 production or import.
risks.early_warning_signals: H2 consumption per barrel > 250 Nm3; makeup H2 compressor running above design capacity; H2 purity in recycle declining
risks.mitigation: Optimise catalyst selectivity to minimise overcracking and methane production; maximise H2 recovery from purge gas via PSA; use higher H2 partial pressure to improve selectivity
risks.contingency: Increase H2 production capacity; import H2 from merchant source; reduce conversion severity to lower H2 consumption

risks.title: Hydrocracker catalyst deactivation
risks.description: Hydrocracking catalyst loses activity over time due to coking, sintering, or poisoning, requiring temperature increase to maintain conversion, eventually leading to end-of-run conditions.
risks.early_warning_signals: Reactor temperature required to maintain conversion rising; product quality endpoints drifting up; catalyst bed delta-P increasing
risks.mitigation: Maintain adequate H2 partial pressure; implement guard bed to remove trace contaminants; design catalyst cycle life of 2-3 years; online catalyst rejuvenation if applicable
risks.contingency: Increase operating temperature within design limits; replace or regenerate catalyst during planned turnaround; install additional guard bed to extend cycle life

risks.title: Wax solidification and plugging in transfer lines
risks.description: High-melting-point FT wax (melting point 80-110°C) solidifies if process lines, filters, or valves cool during reduced throughput or winter conditions, causing blockages.
risks.early_warning_signals: Line pressure drop increasing; trace heat system failing on wax lines; temperature in wax transfer lines approaching wax melting point
risks.mitigation: Steam or electric heat tracing on all wax lines with redundant circuits; insulation specification for winter conditions; maintain minimum flow rates; install wax sumps with steam-out connections
risks.contingency: Steam-out and clear solidified wax lines; increase trace heating capacity; install additional drain points

risks.title: Isomerisation selectivity too low — freeze point not met
risks.description: Hydroisomerisation catalyst produces insufficient branched hydrocarbons, resulting in a jet product freeze point warmer than -47°C specification and failure to meet ASTM D7566 requirements.
risks.early_warning_signals: Product freeze point trending above -47°C; n-paraffin content in jet fraction > 10%; gas chromatography showing low iso/normal ratio
risks.mitigation: Use high-performance Pt-zeolite isomerisation catalyst with optimised pore structure; operate at temperature and pressure that maximises isomerisation over cracking; recycle unconverted n-paraffins
risks.contingency: Reduce reactor throughput and increase severity; replace catalyst with higher-isomerisation selectivity type; blend with isoparaffinic components

risks.title: Product freeze point exceeds -47°C specification
risks.description: FT-SPK jet fuel fails the freeze point specification (> -47°C), making the product non-certifiable as aviation turbine fuel under ASTM D7566.
risks.early_warning_signals: Laboratory freeze point measurements trending toward -47°C; n-paraffin concentration in jet fraction rising; isomerisation reactor performance declining
risks.mitigation: Maintain tight control on hydrocracker/isomeriser conversion; blend with isoparaffinic heavy stream; implement online freeze point analyser for real-time quality control
risks.contingency: Re-run product through hydroisomerisation; blend with approved batch meeting spec; sell as non-aviation diesel if spec not met

risks.title: Product flash point below 38°C specification
risks.description: FT-SPK contains light ends that depress the flash point below the minimum 38°C requirement for Jet A-1, posing a safety and certification issue.
risks.early_warning_signals: Flash point trending below 38°C; distillation front-end (IBP-T10%) lighter than specification; light ends concentration in product increasing
risks.mitigation: Optimise product fractionation cut points; install stripper column to remove light ends; online flash point monitoring with automatic divert
risks.contingency: Re-run product through stabiliser; blend with higher flash point material; reprocess light ends into naphtha pool

risks.title: Product density outside 730-770 kg/m3 range
risks.description: FT-SPK density deviates from the ASTM D7566 specification range of 730-770 kg/m3 at 15°C, caused by incorrect hydrocracking severity or feedstock composition shifts.
risks.early_warning_signals: Density trending below 730 or above 770 kg/m3; distillation curve shifting heavy or light; aromatics content changing
risks.mitigation: Control hydrocracking severity to maintain density within spec; blend batches to average out density variations; online densitometer with feedback to process control
risks.contingency: Blend off-spec product with material of opposite density; re-run through hydroprocessing at adjusted severity; sell as alternative hydrocarbon stream

risks.title: Aromatics content too low (< 8 vol%)
risks.description: FT-SPK is essentially zero-aromatic; while ASTM D7566 allows up to 25 vol% in the blend, the FT-SPK itself must be blended with at least 8 vol% aromatics-containing Jet A-1, and very low aromatics can cause seal-swelling and elastomer compatibility issues.
risks.early_warning_signals: Aromatics concentration below 0.5 vol%; elastomer swelling tests failing; customer feedback on seal compatibility
risks.mitigation: Design product as blend component (max 50% FT-SPK in Jet A-1 ensures adequate aromatics); add aromatic hydrocarbons from biomass-derived sources (e.g., lignin hydroprocessing); test elastomer compatibility with final blend
risks.contingency: Blend with conventional Jet A-1 to raise aromatics to >8 vol%; add synthetic aromatics (alkylated benzenes); market product specification as blend-only component

risks.title: Thermal stability failure — JFTOT test not passed
risks.description: FT-SPK fails the JFTOT (Jet Fuel Thermal Oxidation Test) at 260°C, indicating poor thermal stability, likely due to trace oxygenates, nitrogen compounds, or particulate contamination.
risks.early_warning_signals: JFTOT pressure drop increasing during test; tube deposit rating above 3; visual discolouration of test fluid
risks.mitigation: Ensure deep hydrotreating to remove oxygenates; improve product filtration (0.5 micron final filter); add antioxidant additive before certification testing; maintain nitrogen blanketing in storage
risks.contingency: Re-treat product with additional hydrotreating or clay treatment; blend with certified batch; identify and eliminate contaminant source

risks.title: Blend incompatibility with conventional Jet A-1
risks.description: FT-SPK exhibits incompatibility when blended with certain conventional Jet A-1 sources — phase separation, additive interaction, or particulate formation upon mixing.
risks.early_warning_signals: Haze or sediment forming on blending; filterability test failing; additive package effectiveness reduced in blend
risks.mitigation: Pre-blend compatibility testing with representative Jet A-1 batches; use additive package designed for synthetic blend compatibility; controlled mixing procedure with adequate recirculation
risks.contingency: Adjust blend ratio; change Jet A-1 source; use separate dedicated additive package for the blend

risks.title: Trace contaminants in FT-SPK product
risks.description: Trace levels of sulfur (above 15 ppm), nitrogen, metals (Fe, Co, Ni), or oxygenates in the final product cause specification failure or downstream fuel system issues.
risks.early_warning_signals: Sulfur trending above 10 ppm; metals detected in product GC/ICP analysis; oxygenates above measurable threshold
risks.mitigation: Ensure adequate hydrotreating to remove heteroatoms; final polishing via clay bed or activated carbon; comprehensive product quality monitoring program
risks.contingency: Re-route product through hydrotreater; replace polishing media; segregate and reprocess off-spec material

risks.title: ASTM D7566 FT-SPK Annex certification failure on one or more properties
risks.description: A batch of FT-SPK fails qualification testing per ASTM D7566 Annex A1, preventing certification for aviation use and requiring re-blending or alternative disposition.
risks.early_warning_signals: Pre-certification testing showing marginal results; one or more properties approaching specification limits; batch-to-batch variability increasing
risks.mitigation: Maintain product within ASTM D7566 specification with 20% margin on critical properties; pre-qualify every batch before blending; engage ASTM certification body early in project
risks.contingency: Re-blend off-spec batch to correct properties; blend with certified batch; sell as non-certified industrial fuel

risks.title: ASTM qualification testing timeline slips
risks.description: The ASTM qualification testing programme for FT-SPK (or a new variant) takes longer than planned due to test lab availability, retesting, or specification review delays, postponing first-sale date.
risks.early_warning_signals: Test lab backlogs extending beyond schedule; first-time test failures requiring repeats; ASTM review committee meeting delays
risks.mitigation: Engage multiple qualified test labs; submit samples early for pre-qualification; maintain active engagement with ASTM D02 committee; prepare comprehensive data package
risks.contingency: Use interim certification pathway (e.g., JIG or OEM approval); sell as diesel/heating oil during delay; increase lab testing capacity

risks.title: Blending certification delayed at airport/hub
risks.description: Certification for blending FT-SPK with conventional Jet A-1 at specific airport infrastructure (hydrant systems, storage tanks, truck loading) is delayed due to testing requirements or regulatory approvals.
risks.early_warning_signals: Airport fuel hydrant system compatibility review not initiated; additive compatibility testing incomplete; refinery-to-airport logistics plan not approved
risks.mitigation: Engage airport fuel consortium early; pre-test blend compatibility with airport-specific Jet A-1; prepare blending certification documentation in advance
risks.contingency: Use interim truck-to-plane fuelling bypassing hydrant; certify blending at alternative airport; use dedicated blending facility off-airport

risks.title: FAA/EASA waiver for new fuel pathway not obtained
risks.description: Regulatory approval (FAA/EASA waiver or Annex extension) for the specific FT-SPK pathway is delayed or denied, preventing commercial aviation use.
risks.early_warning_signals: Regulatory submission incomplete; OEM (Boeing, Airbus) testing data insufficient; regulatory agency feedback indicating additional data required
risks.mitigation: Submit complete data package early with all required OEM fit-for-purpose testing; engage regulatory consultants; maintain active dialogue with FAA/EASA fuels specialists
risks.contingency: Pursue interim ASTM D7566 Annex approval for existing FT pathway; market fuel as non-aviation renewable diesel; apply for regulatory support from trade associations

risks.title: Batch-to-batch variation in FT-SPK properties
risks.description: Significant variation in product properties between production batches requires per-batch certification testing, creating operational delays and potential customer acceptance issues.
risks.early_warning_signals: Property RSD% across batches increasing; distillation endpoints varying >10°C; freeze point range >3°C across batches
risks.mitigation: Standardise feedstock blends and process conditions; maintain intermediate storage tanks for blending to average out variations; implement process control on key fractionation parameters
risks.contingency: Blend multiple batches in storage to meet specification; increase quality testing frequency; adjust process conditions between batches

risks.title: Carbon intensity exceeds CORSIA/RSB sustainability threshold
risks.description: Lifecycle carbon intensity of the FT-SPK pathway exceeds the CORSIA sustainability threshold (e.g., > 89.0 gCO2e/MJ relative to baseline) or RSB requirement, making the fuel ineligible for regulatory credit.
risks.early_warning_signals: LCA model showing CI above target; indirect emissions from feedstock collection higher than assessed; process energy consumption above design
risks.mitigation: Optimise process energy efficiency (heat integration, power from syngas); use low-carbon H2 from electrolysis; select low-carbon feedstock logistics (short transport distances); maximise carbon efficiency to liquid products
risks.contingency: Purchase carbon credits to offset excess; change feedstock to lower-carbon alternative; invest in process electrification with renewable power

risks.title: Indirect Land Use Change (ILUC) issues
risks.description: Use of dedicated energy crops for SAF feedstock is contested on ILUC grounds, potentially disqualifying the fuel under EU RED II or CORSIA sustainability criteria.
risks.early_warning_signals: Regulatory developments on ILUC in target markets; NGO campaigns against biomass-based fuels; proposed ILUC factors worsening
risks.mitigation: Use waste and residue feedstocks (forestry residues, agricultural residues) to avoid ILUC; source feedstock from degraded/fallow land; implement certification of sustainable land use practices
risks.contingency: Transition to waste/residue-only feedstock slate; accept lower regulatory credit value if ILUC-deemed; pursue feedstocks from certified low-ILUC risk sources

risks.title: Chain-of-custody gaps in biomass traceability
risks.description: Inability to trace biomass from point of origin through the supply chain to the final fuel product, violating ISCC or RSB chain-of-custody requirements and risking certification.
risks.early_warning_signals: Supplier documentation incomplete; mass balance reconciliation gaps; audit findings on traceability; certification body queries
risks.mitigation: Implement digital traceability system (blockchain or audited database); require certified mass-balance documentation at every supply chain node; conduct supplier audits
risks.contingency: Exclude non-compliant suppliers; implement physical segregation instead of mass balance; accept lower certification scope pending gap remediation

risks.title: Sustainability certification audit failure
risks.description: External audit finds non-compliance with ISCC, RSB, or CORSIA sustainability requirements, leading to certification suspension or revocation and loss of market access.
risks.early_warning_signals: Pre-audit findings unresolved; supplier certification expiring; documentation gaps identified; non-conformance reports not closed
risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous compliance with certification standards; conduct internal annual audits; train staff on certification requirements; retain experienced certification consultant
risks.contingency: Implement corrective action plan within audit timeframe; appeal certification decision; temporary sell product on non-regulated markets

risks.title: Sustainability certification scheme withdrawal or change
risks.description: The recognised sustainability certification scheme (ISCC, RSB) changes requirements or is no longer recognised by regulatory bodies (EU RED, CORSIA), requiring recertification under new scheme.
risks.early_warning_signals: Regulatory proposals for new certification requirements; scheme updating its criteria; mutual recognition agreements changing
risks.mitigation: Certify under multiple recognised schemes simultaneously; monitor regulatory developments through trade associations; design sustainability management system to meet highest standard
risks.contingency: Transition to alternative recognised scheme within transition period; adjust operations for new criteria; accept temporary certification gap

risks.title: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) delay
risks.description: Environmental Impact Assessment process for the FT plant takes longer than planned due to complexity, data requests, or public consultation requirements, delaying construction start.
risks.early_warning_signals: Regulator requesting additional studies; public hearing scheduled late; EIA submission completeness review extended; environmental groups filing objections
risks.mitigation: Commission EIA early with experienced consultants; engage stakeholders and regulators proactively; prepare comprehensive baseline studies; include buffer in project schedule
risks.contingency: Request scoping meeting to narrow study requirements; fund additional studies to address regulator concerns; adjust project boundaries to reduce environmental footprint

risks.title: Public opposition to biomass FT facility
risks.description: Local community or environmental groups oppose the FT plant based on emissions, traffic, feedstock sustainability, or visual impact concerns, leading to permitting delays or legal challenges.
risks.early_warning_signals: Letters of objection filed; local news articles critical of project; community meeting with strong opposition; petition signatures collected
risks.mitigation: Proactive community engagement programme; local benefit sharing (jobs, community fund); transparent communication on emissions and sustainability; site selection away from sensitive receptors
risks.contingency: Increase community benefit package; modify site layout or operations to address concerns; legal defence of permit; consider alternative site

risks.title: Air emissions permit limits too restrictive
risks.description: Regulators impose air emission limits (NOx, SOx, CO, PM, VOCs) below what the FT process can reliably achieve, requiring expensive abatement technology or limiting throughput.
risks.early_warning_signals: Draft permit limits below BACT guidance; regulator citing sensitive receptor modelling; negotiations on emission limits stalling
risks.mitigation: Design emission control systems with 30% margin over expected permit limits; use best available control technology (BACT); engage regulator with robust emissions modelling
risks.contingency: Install additional abatement equipment (SCR, baghouse); reduce plant throughput to meet mass limits; challenge limits through administrative or legal process

risks.title: Wastewater discharge quality permit constraints
risks.description: FT process wastewater (containing oxygenates, alcohols, acids, catalyst fines) requires extensive treatment to meet discharge permit limits, increasing cost and complexity.
risks.early_warning_signals: Draft permit limits more stringent than expected; wastewater characterisation showing higher COD/TOC; regulator requiring zero liquid discharge (ZLD)
risks.mitigation: Design full wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) with biological + tertiary treatment; minimise water usage through recycle; evaluate ZLD if required by local regulation
risks.contingency: Increase WWTP capacity; contract third-party wastewater treatment; increase water recycle and evaporation

risks.title: Hazardous chemical storage/use licence delay
risks.description: Licence for storage and use of hazardous chemicals (H2, CO, syngas, catalysts, solvents) is delayed due to safety review, site inspection findings, or regulatory backlog.
risks.early_warning_signals: Regulatory inspection scheduled late; application completeness review queries; safety report requiring revision
risks.mitigation: Prepare comprehensive safety report (Seveso/COMAH-tier if required); engage regulator early on chemical inventory and risk assessment; design for inherently safer processes
risks.contingency: Reduce onsite chemical storage (more frequent deliveries); use less hazardous alternatives where possible; request temporary operating permit pending full licence

risks.title: Carbon monoxide (CO) toxicity incident in syngas area
risks.description: CO release from syngas piping, compressors, or gasifier due to leak or maintenance error causes toxic exposure to personnel, with potentially fatal consequences.
risks.early_warning_signals: Fixed CO detectors showing elevated readings; maintenance on syngas equipment without proper isolation; near-miss report of CO exposure
risks.mitigation: Fixed CO detection network with alarm and automatic isolation; full-face respirators and SCBA in syngas areas; confined space entry procedures; gas testing before any hot work or entry
risks.contingency: Evacuate and ventilate area; medical treatment for exposure; incident investigation and root cause analysis; review and update procedures

risks.title: Hydrogen flammability and explosion risk
risks.description: Hydrogen leaks from H2 compressors, piping, or storage create high fire/explosion risk due to its wide flammability range (4-75%), low ignition energy, and tendency to leak through seals.
risks.early_warning_signals: H2 detector activations; seal leakage on H2 compressors; near-miss hydrogen events; maintenance on H2 systems without positive isolation
risks.mitigation: H2-specific detection with automatic ventilation and isolation; intrinsically safe equipment in H2 areas; hydrogen-compatible materials for piping (no hydrogen embrittlement risk); strict hot work permit system
risks.contingency: Emergency isolation and depressuring; fire suppression activation; evacuation and area control; root cause investigation

risks.title: FT high-pressure loop (30-40 bar) integrity failure
risks.description: Failure of a pressure component in the FT synthesis loop (reactor, recycle compressor, heat exchangers) operating at 30-40 bar and 200-250°C releases syngas and hydrocarbons.
risks.early_warning_signals: Pressure relief valve lifting frequency increasing; flange leak during start-up/shutdown; inspection finding wall thinning or cracking
risks.mitigation: Design to relevant pressure vessel codes (ASME VIII, EN 13445); regular NDT inspection (UT, RT) at designed intervals; pressure relief system sized for worst-case fire scenario; remote isolation valves
risks.contingency: Emergency shutdown and depressuring; firewater activation if ignited; area evacuation; repair or replace failed component after metallurgical investigation

risks.title: Catalyst pyrophoricity during handling (Co/Fe reduction)
risks.description: Reduced FT catalyst (cobalt or iron in metallic state) is pyrophoric and ignites on exposure to air during loading, unloading, or regeneration, causing fires and potential injuries.
risks.early_warning_signals: Catalyst bed temperature rising after shutdown; air ingress into catalyst hoppers during loading; catalyst fines visible in vents
risks.mitigation: Maintain nitrogen or inert gas blanket during all catalyst handling; slow controlled passivation procedure before catalyst exposure; dedicated catalyst handling procedures and equipment
risks.contingency: Nitrogen purge to smother fire; emergency catalyst dump into nitrogen-purged container; fire suppression with dry chemical (no water on reduced catalyst)

risks.title: Syngas and catalyst fires during maintenance
risks.description: During maintenance turnarounds, residual syngas or pyrophoric catalyst fines in equipment can ignite when equipment is opened, causing fires and potential personnel injury.
risks.early_warning_signals: Incomplete nitrogen purge verification; catalyst fines not wetted or passivated before opening; hydrocarbon analysers showing residual gas detection
risks.mitigation: Positive isolation (blinds or double block-and-bleed) before maintenance; nitrogen purge and gas test before opening; catalyst wetting/passivation procedure before manway entry; continuous gas monitoring during work
risks.contingency: Emergency response activation; back-up inert gas supply; re-purge and re-test before continuing; incident investigation

risks.title: Confined space entry incidents in vessels and tanks
risks.description: Personnel entering FT reactors, gasifiers, storage tanks, or other confined spaces face risks of toxic gas, oxygen deficiency, or engulfment due to residual hydrocarbons or catalyst fines.
risks.early_warning_signals: Confined space permits not followed strictly; atmospheric testing equipment not used; rescue equipment not readily available; near-miss reported
risks.mitigation: Rigorous confined space entry programme — permit, atmospheric testing, continuous monitoring, standby rescue team; all confined spaces identified and labelled; use remote inspection tools (robotics) where possible
risks.contingency: Rescue team activation; emergency medical services; investigation and root cause analysis; retrain all personnel on confined space procedures

risks.title: EPC cost overrun exceeding 15% of budget
risks.description: Engineering, procurement, and construction costs exceed the approved budget by more than 15% due to scope changes, material cost escalation, labour productivity issues, or design errors.
risks.early_warning_signals: Monthly cost reports showing negative variance; change order requests accumulating; material price escalation beyond contingency; engineering hours exceeding budget
risks.mitigation: Lump-sum turnkey EPC contract with well-defined scope; 15-20% contingency in budget; robust change management process; weekly cost/progress reviews with contractor
risks.contingency: Draw on project contingency; reduce scope to core units; negotiate with contractor on shared overrun; secure additional funding

risks.title: EPC schedule slip delaying first production
risks.description: Project completion and first SAF production delayed beyond the planned date due to engineering delays, equipment delivery slippage, construction productivity issues, or weather.
risks.early_warning_signals: Engineering deliverables behind schedule; major equipment (gasifier, FT reactor) delivery milestones slipping; construction productivity below plan; weather days exceeding allowance
risks.mitigation: Realistic schedule with 3-6 months float; early ordering of long-lead items; detailed front-end engineering (FEED) before EPC start; contractor performance incentives and penalties
risks.contingency: Acceleration plan (overtime, additional crews); fast-track remaining engineering; modularisation to shift work off-site; partial commissioning sequence for early production

risks.title: Poor construction quality requiring rework
risks.description: Construction quality failures — welding defects, incorrect material installation, poor concrete work — requiring rework that adds cost and schedule delay.
risks.early_warning_signals: NDT rejection rate above industry norm; quality audit findings increasing; rework hours trending upward; punch list items accumulating
risks.mitigation: Rigorous quality management system; third-party NDT and inspection; contractor qualification and pre-qualification; quality hold points at critical stages
risks.contingency: Accelerate rework with additional crews; replace underperforming subcontractors; increase inspection frequency

risks.title: Contractor insolvency during construction
risks.description: Main EPC contractor or key subcontractor becomes insolvent during construction, causing work stoppage, legal complexity, and costly replacement contracting.
risks.early_warning_signals: Contractor delaying payments to subcontractors; financial reports showing losses; lien filings by subcontractors; key personnel departing
risks.mitigation: Financial due diligence on EPC contractor before award; performance bond and parent company guarantee; milestone-based payment; maintain contingency for contractor replacement
risks.contingency: Step-in rights to manage contract directly; novate subcontracts to replacement contractor; trigger performance bond; engage replacement contractor

risks.title: Labour disputes and workforce strikes
risks.description: Work stoppages due to labour disputes, union action, or workforce dissatisfaction at the construction site, causing schedule delays and cost escalation.
risks.early_warning_signals: Labour union negotiations stalling; grievance filings increasing; workforce turnover rising; competitor sites experiencing disputes
risks.mitigation: Fair labour agreements with clear dispute resolution mechanisms; positive labour relations programme; competitive compensation and benefits; consider project labour agreement (PLA)
risks.contingency: Engage mediation/arbitration; redeploy non-union workforce; recover schedule with overtime after resolution

risks.title: Gasifier long-lead delivery (18-24 months)
risks.description: The gasifier (especially the pressure vessel, internal cyclones, refractory lining) has a fabrication lead time of 18-24 months, driving the critical path and leaving minimal schedule contingency.
risks.early_warning_signals: Vendor order book full; engineering release for gasifier delayed by 2+ months; raw material (specialty steel) procurement delayed
risks.mitigation: Place gasifier order at FID stage (or earlier); select vendor with proven track record and available fabrication capacity; specify standardised design to reduce engineering time
risks.contingency: Expedite fabrication with premium; consider alternative qualified vendor; air-freight critical components; adjust construction sequence if delay unavoidable

risks.title: FT reactor long-lead delivery (18-24 months)
risks.description: The FT reactor (slurry bubble column or multi-tubular fixed bed) requires 18-24 months fabrication due to thick-wall vessel requirements, specialty internals, and rigorous quality testing.
risks.early_warning_signals: Vendor shop capacity nearing full; specialty steel (Cr-Mo) availability issues; nozzle welding qualification delays
risks.mitigation: Order FT reactor early (conditionally before FID if budget allows); pre-qualify multiple fabricators; design with proven fabrication methods and standardised dimensions
risks.contingency: Split fabrication across multiple vendors; expedite critical path items; use modular construction to parallelise work

risks.title: Catalyst supply constrained or single-source
risks.description: FT catalyst (cobalt or iron) and hydroprocessing catalyst are available from a limited number of suppliers, creating supply risk, pricing power, and lead time issues.
risks.early_warning_signals: Catalyst supplier lead times extending; supplier allocating limited production; new SAF facilities competing for same catalyst; price increases notified
risks.mitigation: Qualify at least two catalyst suppliers; enter long-term supply agreement with volume commitments and price formula; hold strategic catalyst inventory (one full charge plus 50%
risks.contingency: Activate secondary supplier; extend current catalyst life through milder operation; use alternative catalyst formulation (iron instead of cobalt if feasible)

risks.title: Sole-source vendor for proprietary equipment
risks.description: Key proprietary equipment (gasifier burner, FT reactor internals, wax filter, specialty compressor) is available only from a single supplier, creating commercial leverage and supply risk.
risks.early_warning_signals: Vendor unable to meet delivery schedule; pricing above budget; vendor not responsive to technical queries; no alternative qualified supplier
risks.mitigation: Verify vendor fabrication capacity and financial health; include liquidated damages for late delivery; negotiate sparing philosophy and aftermarket support agreement; explore second-source pre-qualification
risks.contingency: Expedite with premium payments; use interim/rental equipment if available; accept delivery delay and adjust construction sequence

risks.title: Logistics disruption for heavy/specialised equipment
risks.description: Transport of oversized equipment (gasifier vessel, FT reactor, columns) to site is disrupted by port strikes, road permit issues, bridge/road restrictions, or weather, delaying arrival.
risks.early_warning_signals: Permit for abnormal load not obtained; route survey identifying obstacles; port congestion notifications; weather window constraints
risks.mitigation: Route survey and permit applications well in advance; select site with good transport infrastructure; design for modularisation where possible; contract with experienced heavy-lift logistics provider
risks.contingency: Alternative route planning; use rail or barge instead of road; split vessel into pieces for field assembly

risks.title: Offtake agreement not secured before FID
risks.description: Failure to secure binding long-term offtake agreements for SAF before final investment decision, making financing difficult and project economics uncertain.
risks.early_warning_signals: Airlines delaying SAF purchase commitments; offered price below project breakeven; offtake negotiations stalling on terms; competitors signing agreements ahead
risks.mitigation: Engage multiple airlines and fuel traders early; offer flexible terms (volume, delivery, premium indexation); provide product samples for certification; leverage blending mandate obligations of airlines
risks.contingency: Bridge financing to cover period without offtake; sell on spot market at potentially lower price; pursue government offtake guarantee programme

risks.title: SAF price collapse below breakeven
risks.description: Market price for SAF drops below project breakeven cost due to oversupply, crude oil price collapse, blending mandate relaxation, or emergence of cheaper alternative fuel pathways.
risks.early_warning_signals: Crude oil price declining rapidly; SAF premium over Jet A-1 shrinking; announcements of multiple new SAF plants; policy changes weakening mandate
risks.mitigation: Secure long-term offtake with price floor/minimum premium; produce drop-in fuel with dual revenue streams (SAF + renewable diesel); minimise production cost through efficiency and scale
risks.contingency: Switch product slate to maximise diesel/heating oil when SAF margin low; hedge crude and product prices; reduce operating rate to match market demand

risks.title: Blending mandate implementation delayed or weakened
risks.description: Government SAF blending mandates (ReFuelEU, CORSIA, state-level) are delayed, weakened, or grandfathering provisions limited, reducing the regulatory driver for SAF demand.
risks.early_warning_signals: Legislative process stalling; industry lobbying to delay targets; election results in anti-mandate governments; compliance flexibility being discussed
risks.mitigation: Diversify target markets across multiple regulatory jurisdictions; produce beyond minimum mandated volumes initially; engage in policy advocacy through trade associations
risks.contingency: Sell SAF in voluntary market; redirect product to renewable diesel market; export to region with stronger mandates

risks.title: Airport blending and distribution infrastructure not ready
risks.description: Airports lack the infrastructure (storage tanks, hydrant system upgrades, blending equipment, dedicated delivery) to receive and blend FT-SPK with Jet A-1, delaying market access.
risks.early_warning_signals: Airport fuel consortium not approving infrastructure investment; capital expenditure by airport deferred; logistics study showing infrastructure gaps
risks.mitigation: Engage airport operators and fuel consortia early on infrastructure planning; invest in dedicated storage and blending at airport if needed; use truck-to-wing delivery as interim solution
risks.contingency: Deliver to off-airport blending facility; use multi-modal transport (barge, rail, truck); blend at producer site and deliver as finished blend

risks.title: Catalyst regeneration frequency higher than design
risks.description: FT and hydroprocessing catalysts require regeneration or replacement more frequently than design basis (e.g., every 12 months instead of 24), increasing operating cost and reducing on-stream factor.
risks.early_warning_signals: Catalyst activity declining faster than expected; delta-P across reactor beds rising; product selectivity shifting; regeneration interval below warranty
risks.mitigation: Monitor catalyst performance with online activity tracking; protect catalyst with adequate guard beds; operate within catalyst vendor's recommended parameters; hold spare catalyst charge
risks.contingency: Accelerate catalyst changeout schedule; optimise regeneration procedure; negotiate warranty claim with catalyst vendor; accept higher operating cost

risks.title: Wax handling and transfer system plugging
risks.description: FT wax solidifies, accumulates, or forms deposits in transfer lines, filters, pumps, and storage tanks, causing blockages and requiring frequent cleaning (steam-out, pigging).
risks.early_warning_signals: Wax pump discharge pressure rising; transfer line temperature trending down; filter differential pressure increasing; wax tank heating coil fouling
risks.mitigation: Maintain heat tracing and insulation on all wax systems; design self-draining piping with steam-out connections; install in-line filtration with automatic back-flush
risks.contingency: Steam-out and mechanically clean blocked lines; replace plugged filter elements; add chemical dispersant to wax system

risks.title: Unscheduled maintenance downtime exceeding design allowance
risks.description: Plant availability falls below design target (e.g., < 330 operating days/year) due to unplanned shutdowns from equipment failures, process upsets, or feedstock issues.
risks.early_warning_signals: Failure frequency across plant increasing; mean time between failures (MTBF) declining; reliability metrics below industry benchmark
risks.mitigation: Implement reliability-centred maintenance (RCM) programme; maintain critical spares inventory; install online condition monitoring (vibration, thermography, corrosion monitoring); conduct root cause analysis for each failure
risks.contingency: Prioritise and expedite repairs; use temporary equipment or bypass to continue partial operation; reschedule planned maintenance to recover lost production

risks.title: Spare parts availability insufficient for critical equipment
risks.description: Long lead times for critical spare parts (gasifier feed nozzles, compressor seals, FT reactor internals, special valves) result in extended downtime when failures occur.
risks.early_warning_signals: Vendor quoted lead times > 6 months for critical spares; spares not carried in stock by vendor; budget constraints limiting spare parts purchase
risks.mitigation: Identify critical sparing philosophy in FEED; maintain capital spares inventory for long-lead items; establish framework agreements with original equipment manufacturers for priority supply
risks.contingency: Source alternative parts from other vendors; cannibalise from less critical equipment; emergency fabrication with expedited delivery

risks.title: Project funding not closed at FID
risks.description: Inability to secure project financing (debt, equity, or grants) at final investment decision due to perceived technology risk, offtake not secured, or unfavourable market conditions.
risks.early_warning_signals: Debt term sheets not received; equity investors requiring higher returns; due diligence revealing gaps; credit rating below investment grade thresholds
risks.mitigation: Secure offtake agreements first; engage with multiple lenders (commercial banks, ECAs, DFIs, green funds); prepare comprehensive project information memorandum; strong sponsor support
risks.contingency: Seek government loan guarantees or grants; reduce project scale to match available equity; phased development approach; pursue joint venture partnership with stronger balance sheet partner

risks.title: Project cost escalation exceeding 20% of budget
risks.description: Overall project capital cost escalation exceeds 20% due to inflation, commodity price spikes (steel, nickel, copper), labour shortages, or EPC contractor claims, making the project uneconomic.
risks.early_warning_signals: Engineering cost indices rising; steel/copper/nickel price increases; labour wage inflation in construction sector; EPC change orders accumulating
risks.mitigation: Index-based escalation clauses in EPC contracts; 25% contingency for persistent cost escalation scenarios; fixed-price lump-sum contracts; early procurement of long-lead materials
risks.contingency: Re-base project economics at higher cost; seek additional equity or reduce debt; scope reduction to stay within budget; defer non-essential units to phase 2

risks.title: Adverse foreign exchange rate movement
risks.description: Exchange rate depreciation (if project has foreign currency debt or imports significant equipment/materials priced in foreign currency) increases project cost in local currency terms.
risks.early_warning_signals: Currency depreciation trend in project country; central bank policy changes; trade deficit widening; political instability affecting currency
risks.mitigation: Denominate debt and revenue in same currency where possible; hedge FX exposure through forwards/options; negotiate local content to reduce foreign expenditure
risks.contingency: Draw on FX hedging contracts; restructure debt to match currency profile; accelerate revenue generation in foreign currency

risks.title: Tariff changes affecting feedstock or product economics
risks.description: Changes in import/export tariffs on biomass feedstock, catalysts, or SAF products due to trade policy changes disrupt the project's competitive cost position.
risks.early_warning_signals: Trade disputes involving key trade partners; retaliatory tariff announcements; World Trade Organization challenges; customs reclassification of products
risks.mitigation: Domestic sourcing of feedstock to minimise import exposure; locate production in target market to avoid product tariffs; include tariff escalation clauses in offtake agreements
risks.contingency: Adjust supply chain to avoid tariff-impacted routes; seek tariff exemptions or duty drawback; renegotiate offtake terms to share tariff impact
